text:
Incident Bot: PAGER: high error-rate detected for org=relayorg (eu-west-1). 5xx spike, autotopology noticing GPU saturation, cluster latency up. link: https://incidents.redwood/internal/6123459999

Amy (on-call): seeing it. joining. any customer flags?

Janet Support: RelayOrg reports users hitting timeouts in their web UI. They say it's intermittent but widespread. CS is on the phone.

Mark SRE: quick metrics: relayorg qps -> 4.8x baseline, 5xx rate 12% (was <0.5%), avg p95 latency from inference nodes 3.2s -> 9.7s. Token ingestion is heavily skewed to embedding endpoint /v1/embeddings, long inputs.

Leo Prod Eng: confirmed — their background ingestion job started a backfill concurrently with normal user traffic. it’s saturating KV cache and causing GC pressure.

Amy (on-call): impact to other orgs?

Mark SRE: cross-org tail latency rising in eu-west-1; autoscaler dipping but pods holding. risk: cascade to dedicated pool owners.

Tanya CS: RelayOrg is on a critical rollout, raising urgent revenue/ops concern. they asked for a temporary fix to avoid their customers failing over.

Amy (on-call): propose: apply a short-lived, targeted fairness policy: (1) temporarily bump RelayOrg burst cap on the dedicated pool for 5 minutes to let in-flight user traffic finish, (2) concurrently disable embeddings endpoint for their background backfill job (non-interactive), (3) add a short per-minute quota for non-interactive keys. will revert automatically. any objections?

Mark SRE: agree. alternative is org-wide hard-throttle which will break their rollout. targeted bump + feature disable seems safest. note: need an audit log and timeline.

Leo Prod Eng: commands ready. will run after ✅ from Amy. snippet:
```
# bump qps for relayorg for 300s
redwoodctl org adjust-rate relayorg --qps 1800 --burst 3500 --duration 300
# disable embeddings for relayorg (non-interactive jobs)
redwoodctl org set-feature relayorg embeddings --state disabled --reason "emergency backfill mitigation"
```

Janet Support: i’ll message RelayOrg account contact with ETA and rollback plan. they should avoid re-queueing the backfill while we run this.

Amy (on-call): do it. Mark, please ensure a revert job scheduled. record start ts.

DeployBot: Action accepted. Executing change: adjust-rate(relayorg) -> qps:1800, burst:3500, ttl:300s. request id: dbf-7c9a

DeployBot: Feature toggle: embeddings disabled for org=relayorg. request id: dbf-7c9b

Mark SRE: changes applied. cluster metrics starting to normalize. 5xx down to 3.1% within 45s, p95 to 4.1s. still monitoring.

Tanya CS: RelayOrg on call says their UI errors dropped to near-zero. they appreciate the quick turnaround.

Amy (on-call): leaving a note — this bump will be automatically reverted at +300s. if anything regresses, we will re-open. assign follow-up postmortem to Mark + Leo + Janet.

Mark SRE: scheduling follow-up: root cause = concurrent backfill + insufficient isolation on embeddings path. mitigation actions: org-specific burst quotas, improved feature gating controls, and a fail-open backpressure queue.

Janet Support: logged customer comms and billing note (temporary overage credit?), CS will follow up on billing.

DeployBot: Revert scheduled. pending revert at ts=6123460299 -> executing revert now. request id: dbf-7c9c

DeployBot: Revert complete. rate/burst restored to policy baseline, embeddings feature restored. request id: dbf-7c9d

Amy (on-call): closing the paging loop. please add the timeline and commands to the incident doc: https://incidents.redwood/internal/6123459999/overview

Tanya CS: noted. will flag as high-priority customer follow-up.

Mark SRE: created a short eval to prevent background backfills from hitting embeddings endpoint without explicit quota reservation.

Amy (on-call): thanks all. :thumbsup:

(Incident thread ends)
__notes: single-thread Slack export: messages in chronological order, prefixed by sender name. metadata fields required by agents.md are present.
